items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขอร้องและการตอบรับคำขอร้อง

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I buy a drink?
B: ______
choices: Yes, my eyes are fine, thanks.
No problem, I'll drink it for you.

explanation.en: "Keep an eye on" means "watch or look after", so agreeing to help with "Sure, take your time" is the natural reply. "My eyes are fine" takes the idiom literally, and "Never mind, it doesn't matter" answers an apology, not a request.
explanation.th: "keep an eye on" แปลว่า ช่วยดูแลหรือเฝ้าให้ คำตอบที่เหมาะคือ "Sure, take your time." (ได้เลย ไม่ต้องรีบ) ส่วน "my eyes are fine" แปลสำนวนตรงตัว และ "Never mind, it doesn't matter" ใช้ตอบคำขอโทษ ไม่ใช่คำขอร้อง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขอโทษและการตอบรับคำขอโทษ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: I'm so sorry — I forgot to bring the book you lent me.
B: ______
A: Thanks. I'll bring it tomorrow, I promise.
choices: That's right. You should forget it.
Don't worry about it. There's no rush.
You're welcome. I'm glad you liked it.
I'm sorry too. It was my fault.

explanation.en: A apologises, then thanks B, so B must accept the apology kindly: "Don't worry about it. There's no rush." "You're welcome" answers thanks, not an apology, and B did nothing wrong, so "It was my fault" makes no sense.
explanation.th: A ขอโทษแล้วขอบคุณ B ดังนั้น B ต้องตอบรับคำขอโทษอย่างใจดี คือ "Don't worry about it. There's no rush." ส่วน "You're welcome" ใช้ตอบคำขอบคุณ และ B ไม่ได้ทำผิด จึงพูดว่า "It was my fault" ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับและปฏิเสธคำเชิญอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: We're having a barbecue on Saturday. Would you like to come?
B: ______ I've already promised to help my aunt move house.
choices: Yes, I'd be glad to come.
No, I wouldn't like to come at all.
I'd love to, but I'm afraid I can't.
I'm not sure whether you'll come.

explanation.en: B's next sentence gives a reason for saying no, so B needs a polite refusal: "I'd love to, but I'm afraid I can't." "Yes, I'd be glad to come" contradicts the reason, and "No, I wouldn't like to come at all" is rude.
explanation.th: ประโยคถัดไปของ B ให้เหตุผลที่ไปไม่ได้ จึงต้องปฏิเสธอย่างสุภาพว่า "I'd love to, but I'm afraid I can't." ส่วน "Yes, I'd be glad to come" ขัดกับเหตุผล และ "No, I wouldn't like to come at all" ฟังดูหยาบคาย

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเข้าใจสำนวนในบทสนทนา

topic.th: บทสนทนา: สำนวนและวลีที่ใช้บ่อย

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: How did your driving test go?
B: Honestly, it was a piece of cake.
A: ______
choices: That's a shame. Was it very difficult?
Never mind. You can take it again next month.
Great! I knew you'd pass easily.
Oh no, did you feel hungry during the test?

explanation.en: "A piece of cake" means "very easy", so A congratulates B: "Great! I knew you'd pass easily." The hunger reply takes the idiom literally; "That's a shame" and "take it again" wrongly suggest B failed.
explanation.th: "a piece of cake" เป็นสำนวน แปลว่า ง่ายมาก A จึงควรแสดงความยินดีว่า "Great! I knew you'd pass easily." ส่วนคำตอบเรื่องหิวแปลสำนวนตรงตัว และ "That's a shame" กับ "take it again" เข้าใจผิดว่า B สอบตก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขอและการให้คำแนะนำ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: I've got a terrible headache, and I still have two chapters to read.
B: ______
choices: Why don't you reading them later?
If I were you, I'd take a short break first.
I'd rather you have a headache.

explanation.en: "If I were you, I'd …" is a correct and natural way to give advice. "You'd better" is followed by the base form (not "to read"), "Why don't you" also takes the base form (not "reading"), and "I'd rather you have a headache" is not advice.
explanation.th: "If I were you, I'd …" เป็นรูปแบบการให้คำแนะนำที่ถูกต้อง ส่วน "You'd better" ต้องตามด้วยกริยาช่องหนึ่ง ไม่ใช่ "to read" และ "Why don't you" ก็ตามด้วยกริยาช่องหนึ่ง ไม่ใช่ "reading" ส่วน "I'd rather you have a headache" ไม่ใช่คำแนะนำ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแสดงความเห็นด้วยและไม่เห็นด้วยอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: I think schools should ban mobile phones completely.
B: ______ Phones can be really useful for research in class.
choices: Exactly, that's what I think too.
I see your point, but I'm not sure I agree.

explanation.en: B goes on to defend phones, so B is disagreeing politely: "I see your point, but I'm not sure I agree." "I couldn't agree more" and "Exactly" show full agreement, and "So do I" also agrees (and sounds odd after "I think … should").
explanation.th: B พูดต่อว่าโทรศัพท์มีประโยชน์ แสดงว่า B ไม่เห็นด้วยอย่างสุภาพ คือ "I see your point, but I'm not sure I agree." ส่วน "I couldn't agree more" และ "Exactly" แปลว่าเห็นด้วยอย่างยิ่ง และ "So do I" ก็แสดงการเห็นด้วยเช่นกัน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การขออนุญาตและการอนุญาต

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: Do you mind if I open the window? It's quite hot in here.
B: ______

explanation.en: "Do you mind if …?" asks whether B objects. To give permission we answer "No" or "Not at all", so "Not at all. Go ahead." is right. Answering "Yes" actually means "I do mind", which clashes with "please open it" and "I don't mind".
explanation.th: "Do you mind if …?" ถามว่า B รังเกียจหรือไม่ ถ้าจะอนุญาตต้องตอบปฏิเสธ เช่น "Not at all. Go ahead." การตอบ "Yes" หมายความว่ารังเกียจ จึงขัดกับ "please open it" และ "I don't mind"

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Checking understanding and asking for clarification
skill.th: การตรวจสอบความเข้าใจและการขอคำอธิบาย

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ภาษาที่ใช้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the conversation.
A: The meeting has been brought forward to Thursday.
B: ______
A: No, earlier. It was on Friday; now it's on Thursday.
choices: Sorry, do you mean it's been moved later?
Great, so we have one more day to prepare.
Sorry, could you speak more slowly?

explanation.en: A answers "No, earlier", so B must have checked whether the meeting was moved later: "Sorry, do you mean it's been moved later?" "Bring forward" means "move to an earlier time". "One more day to prepare" is the wrong meaning and does not lead to A's reply.
explanation.th: A ตอบว่า "No, earlier" แสดงว่า B ถามเพื่อตรวจสอบว่าเลื่อนออกไปช้ากว่าเดิมใช่ไหม คือ "Sorry, do you mean it's been moved later?" (bring forward แปลว่า เลื่อนให้เร็วขึ้น) ส่วน "one more day to prepare" เข้าใจความหมายผิดและไม่สอดคล้องกับคำตอบของ A

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Choosing the word that fits the context
skill.th: การเลือกคำให้เหมาะกับบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The museum is closed today, so we'll have to ______ our visit until next week."

explanation.en: "Postpone" means "move to a later time", which matches "until next week". "Prevent" means "stop something happening", "pretend" means "act as if", and "propose" means "suggest".
explanation.th: "postpone" แปลว่า เลื่อนออกไป เข้ากับ "until next week" ส่วน "prevent" แปลว่า ป้องกัน "pretend" แปลว่า แกล้งทำ และ "propose" แปลว่า เสนอ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้คำที่ใช้คู่กันอย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"We were late for the film because of the ______ traffic on the main road."

explanation.en: English says "heavy traffic" for a lot of traffic. "Strong", "big" and "thick" do not collocate with "traffic".
explanation.th: ภาษาอังกฤษใช้ "heavy traffic" หมายถึง รถติดหนาแน่น คำว่า "strong", "big" และ "thick" ไม่ใช้คู่กับ "traffic"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้กริยาวลี (phrasal verbs)

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The outdoor concert was ______ because the singer had a sore throat."

explanation.en: "Call off" means "cancel", which fits the reason given. "Call up" means "telephone", "put on" means "organise a show", and "take off" means "remove" or "leave the ground".
explanation.th: "call off" แปลว่า ยกเลิก เข้ากับเหตุผลที่นักร้องเจ็บคอ ส่วน "call up" แปลว่า โทรหา "put on" แปลว่า จัดการแสดง และ "take off" แปลว่า ถอดออก หรือ (เครื่องบิน) ขึ้น

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Finding a word with a similar meaning
skill.th: การหาคำที่มีความหมายใกล้เคียง

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word closest in meaning to "reluctant" in this sentence.
"The new manager was reluctant to change the rules so soon after arriving."

explanation.en: "Reluctant" means "not wanting to do something", so "unwilling" is closest. "Eager" is the opposite, and "unable" means "cannot", not "does not want to".
explanation.th: "reluctant" แปลว่า ไม่เต็มใจ จึงใกล้เคียงกับ "unwilling" มากที่สุด ส่วน "eager" มีความหมายตรงข้าม (กระตือรือร้น) และ "unable" แปลว่า ทำไม่ได้ ไม่ใช่ ไม่อยากทำ

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Forming words with prefixes and suffixes
skill.th: การสร้างคำด้วยอุปสรรคและปัจจัย

topic.th: คำศัพท์: การสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The flood caused ______ damage to farms in the north, and many families lost their whole harvest."

explanation.en: An adjective meaning "large in amount" is needed before "damage": "considerable". "Considerate" means "kind and thoughtful", "considering" is a verb form or preposition, and "consideration" is a noun.
explanation.th: ต้องใช้คำคุณศัพท์ที่แปลว่า มากพอสมควร ขยาย "damage" คือ "considerable" ส่วน "considerate" แปลว่า เกรงใจ มีน้ำใจ "considering" เป็นรูปกริยาหรือบุพบท และ "consideration" เป็นคำนาม

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Choosing the word that fits the context
skill.th: การเลือกคำให้เหมาะกับบริบท

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The results of the survey were ______: half the students liked the new timetable and half did not."

explanation.en: An even split gives no clear answer, so the results were "inconclusive". "Unanimous" means everyone agreed, "conclusive" means clear and final, and "inevitable" means "certain to happen".
explanation.th: ผลแบ่งครึ่งต่อครึ่งจึงสรุปไม่ได้ ใช้ "inconclusive" ส่วน "unanimous" แปลว่า เป็นเอกฉันท์ "conclusive" แปลว่า ชัดเจนสรุปได้ และ "inevitable" แปลว่า หลีกเลี่ยงไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Finding a word with the opposite meaning
skill.th: การหาคำที่มีความหมายตรงข้าม

topic.th: คำศัพท์: ความหมายตามบริบท

items.stem:
Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to "generous".
"Our neighbour is very generous; she often shares fruit from her garden with everyone in the street."

explanation.en: "Generous" means "happy to give"; the opposite is "stingy" (unwilling to give or spend). "Humble", "honest" and "cheerful" are other positive qualities, not opposites.
explanation.th: "generous" แปลว่า ใจกว้าง ชอบให้ คำตรงข้ามคือ "stingy" (ขี้เหนียว) ส่วน "humble" (ถ่อมตัว) "honest" (ซื่อสัตย์) และ "cheerful" (ร่าเริง) ไม่ใช่คำตรงข้าม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้กริยาวลี (phrasal verbs)

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"I can't ______ the noise from the building site any longer. I'm going to complain to the council."

explanation.en: "Put up with" means "tolerate", which fits "any longer" and the decision to complain. "Put off" means "delay", "get over" means "recover from", and "look down on" means "think someone is inferior".
explanation.th: "put up with" แปลว่า ทนต่อ เข้ากับ "any longer" และการตัดสินใจร้องเรียน ส่วน "put off" แปลว่า เลื่อน "get over" แปลว่า ทำใจ/หายจาก และ "look down on" แปลว่า ดูถูก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้คำที่ใช้คู่กันอย่างเป็นธรรมชาติ

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Teenagers need to ______ a balance between schoolwork and rest."

explanation.en: The fixed expression is "strike a balance", meaning "find a sensible middle point". "Hit", "take" and "push" do not collocate with "a balance" in this meaning.
explanation.th: สำนวนที่ถูกคือ "strike a balance" แปลว่า หาจุดสมดุล ส่วน "hit", "take" และ "push" ไม่ใช้คู่กับ "a balance" ในความหมายนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้กริยาวลี (phrasal verbs)

topic.th: คำศัพท์: คำที่ใช้คู่กันและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Please ______ this form in black ink and return it to the school office."

explanation.en: You "fill in" a form (write the information in the spaces). "Fill up" is used for containers or a fuel tank, and "full in" and "fill on" are not English phrases.
explanation.th: ใช้ "fill in" กับแบบฟอร์ม หมายถึง กรอกข้อมูล ส่วน "fill up" ใช้กับการเติมให้เต็ม เช่น ถังน้ำมัน และ "full in", "fill on" ไม่มีในภาษาอังกฤษ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การใช้ present perfect กับ past simple

topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: กาลและประโยค passive

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I ______ to Phuket three times, but I've never been to Krabi."

explanation.en: "Three times" with no finished time, plus "I've never been", shows life experience, so the present perfect "have been" is needed. "Went" needs a finished past time, and "had gone" needs a later past reference point.
explanation.th: "three times" โดยไม่ระบุเวลาในอดีต และ "I've never been" แสดงประสบการณ์ จึงใช้ present perfect คือ "have been" ส่วน "went" ต้องมีเวลาในอดีตที่ชัดเจน และ "had gone" ต้องมีเหตุการณ์อดีตอีกเหตุการณ์มาอ้างอิง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไข (if-clauses)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If it ______ tomorrow, we'll have the class party indoors."

explanation.en: A first conditional uses the present simple in the if-clause and "will" in the main clause: "If it rains …, we'll …". We do not use "will" after "if" here.
explanation.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขแบบที่ 1 ใช้ present simple ใน if-clause และ will ในประโยคหลัก คือ "If it rains …, we'll …" ไม่ใช้ will หลัง if

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไข (if-clauses)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If I ______ more free time, I would learn to play the guitar."

explanation.en: "Would learn" shows an imaginary present situation (second conditional), so the if-clause needs the past simple: "If I had more free time".
explanation.th: "would learn" แสดงสถานการณ์สมมติในปัจจุบัน (เงื่อนไขแบบที่ 2) if-clause จึงใช้ past simple คือ "If I had more free time"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไข (if-clauses)

topic.en: Grammar: conditionals, clauses and reported speech
topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: ประโยคเงื่อนไข อนุประโยค และ reported speech

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If she ______ the earlier bus, she wouldn't have missed the start of the exam."

explanation.en: "Wouldn't have missed" shows an unreal past (third conditional), so the if-clause needs the past perfect: "had caught".
explanation.th: "wouldn't have missed" แสดงเงื่อนไขที่ไม่เป็นจริงในอดีต (แบบที่ 3) if-clause จึงใช้ past perfect คือ "had caught"

items.subject: eng

skill.th: รูปอนาคต รวมถึง future perfect

topic.th: ไวยากรณ์: กาลและประโยค passive

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The new bridge ______ by the end of next year, so the journey to the city will be much shorter."

explanation.en: "By the end of next year" calls for the future perfect, and a bridge is completed by people, so it must be passive: "will have been completed". "Will complete" and "has completed" are active and need an object.
explanation.th: "by the end of next year" ต้องใช้ future perfect และสะพานถูกสร้างให้เสร็จ จึงต้องเป็น passive คือ "will have been completed" ส่วน "will complete" และ "has completed" เป็น active ต้องมีกรรม

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The girl ______ bicycle was stolen reported it to the police."

explanation.en: The bicycle belongs to the girl, so the possessive relative pronoun "whose" is needed before the noun "bicycle".

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
She asked me, "Where did you buy your shoes?"
"She asked me where ______ my shoes."

explanation.en: In a reported question the word order is like a statement (subject before verb), and the past simple moves back to the past perfect: "where I had bought". "Did I buy" and "had I bought" keep question word order.
explanation.th: คำถามแบบ reported speech ต้องเรียงแบบประโยคบอกเล่า (ประธานก่อนกริยา) และ past simple เลื่อนเป็น past perfect จึงได้ "where I had bought" ส่วน "did I buy" และ "had I bought" ยังเรียงแบบคำถาม

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I'm really looking forward to ______ you at the party on Saturday."

explanation.en: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: "looking forward to seeing".

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Not only ______ the exam, but she also got the highest score in her class."

explanation.en: When a sentence begins with "Not only", the subject and auxiliary are inverted, as in a question: "Not only did she pass …".
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นประโยคด้วย "Not only" ต้องสลับกริยาช่วยกับประธานแบบประโยคคำถาม คือ "Not only did she pass …"

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"You ______ have told me it was your birthday! I would have bought you a present."

explanation.en: "Should have + past participle" criticises something that did not happen in the past. "Must have" expresses a logical conclusion, not a criticism, and "can have" is not used this way.
explanation.th: "should have + V3" ใช้ตำหนิว่าควรจะทำแต่ไม่ได้ทำในอดีต ส่วน "must have" ใช้สรุปอย่างมั่นใจว่าน่าจะเกิดขึ้นแล้ว ไม่ใช่การตำหนิ และ "can have" ไม่ใช้ในความหมายนี้

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I wish I ______ so much cake last night. Now I feel terrible."

explanation.en: A regret about the past ("last night") uses "wish + past perfect": "I wish I hadn't eaten". "Wish + past simple" is for present situations.
explanation.th: การเสียดายเรื่องในอดีต ("last night") ใช้ wish + past perfect คือ "I wish I hadn't eaten" ส่วน wish + past simple ใช้กับสถานการณ์ในปัจจุบัน

items.passage:
When the students of a secondary school in Nonthaburi first suggested turning their empty rooftop into a vegetable garden, many teachers were doubtful. The roof was hot, windy and difficult to (1) ______, and nobody was sure who would look after it during the holidays. However, the students were determined. They (2) ______ a detailed plan, measured the space and asked a local farmer for advice.

The farmer explained that most vegetables need at least six hours of sunlight a day, (3) ______ was not a problem on the roof. The real challenge was water. (4) ______ carrying heavy buckets up four floors, the students designed a simple system that collects rainwater from the roof itself and stores it in large tanks.

Within six months, the garden was producing lettuce, morning glory and chillies. The school canteen now buys the vegetables at a fair price, and the money is used to (5) ______ seeds and tools. Teachers have noticed other benefits, too. Students who used to (6) ______ no interest in science lessons now talk enthusiastically about soil, insects and weather.

The project has not been (7) ______ difficulties. During the long dry season, the tanks sometimes run empty, and a storm last year damaged several plant beds. Yet each problem has taught the students something new. As one fifteen-year-old member put it, "We didn't just grow vegetables. We grew (8) ______ in ourselves."
items.stem: Which choice best fits blank (1)?

explanation.en: "Reach" takes a direct object: "difficult to reach (the roof)". "Arrive" needs "at", "get" needs "to", and "access to" is not a verb phrase here.
explanation.th: "reach" ตามด้วยกรรมได้ทันที "difficult to reach" (ขึ้นไปถึงได้ยาก) ส่วน "arrive" ต้องมี "at" "get" ต้องมี "to" และ "access to" ใช้เป็นกริยาในตำแหน่งนี้ไม่ได้

When the students of a secondary school in Nonthaburi first suggested turning their empty rooftop into a vegetable garden, many teachers were doubtful. The roof was hot, windy and difficult to (1) ______, and nobody was sure who would look after it during the holidays. However, the students were determined. They (2) ______ a detailed plan, measured the space and asked a local farmer for advice.

The farmer explained that most vegetables need at least six hours of sunlight a day, (3) ______ was not a problem on the roof. The real challenge was water. (4) ______ carrying heavy buckets up four floors, the students designed a simple system that collects rainwater from the roof itself and stores it in large tanks.

Within six months, the garden was producing lettuce, morning glory and chillies. The school canteen now buys the vegetables at a fair price, and the money is used to (5) ______ seeds and tools. Teachers have noticed other benefits, too. Students who used to (6) ______ no interest in science lessons now talk enthusiastically about soil, insects and weather.

The project has not been (7) ______ difficulties. During the long dry season, the tanks sometimes run empty, and a storm last year damaged several plant beds. Yet each problem has taught the students something new. As one fifteen-year-old member put it, "We didn't just grow vegetables. We grew (8) ______ in ourselves."
items.stem: Which choice best fits blank (7)?

explanation.en: "Not without difficulties" means "it did have some difficulties", which the next sentences describe. "Beyond", "except" and "apart" do not make sense here.

items.passage:
Why Teenagers Can't Fall Asleep Early

Parents often complain that their teenage children stay up too late at night and then struggle to get out of bed in the morning. It is easy to blame smartphones or laziness, but scientists say the real story is more complicated.

During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts. Melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy, is released about two hours later in teenagers than in younger children or adults. As a result, a fifteen-year-old who goes to bed at ten o'clock may simply lie awake, staring at the ceiling, for a long time. This change is biological, not a matter of choice, and it appears in teenagers all over the world.

The problem is that school timetables do not take this shift into account. Many schools start before eight o'clock, which means students must wake up while their bodies still think it is the middle of the night. Researchers estimate that most teenagers need between eight and ten hours of sleep, yet surveys suggest that the majority get fewer than seven on school nights. The consequences go beyond feeling tired. Lack of sleep has been linked to poor concentration, low mood and even a higher risk of road accidents among young drivers.

Some schools have experimented with later start times. In one well-known study, a group of schools moved the start of the day from 7.50 to 8.30. Within a year, attendance improved, fewer students fell asleep in class, and average grades rose slightly. Not everyone was pleased, however. Some parents found it harder to organise their working day, and sports coaches complained that training sessions had to finish later in the evening.

Screens do play a part, of course. The blue light from phones and tablets can delay the release of melatonin even further. Experts therefore suggest that teenagers switch off their devices at least an hour before bed. But they also warn that advice alone will not solve the problem. Unless schools and families recognise that teenage sleep patterns are different, young people will continue to start each day with a sleep debt they can never fully repay.
items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Smartphones are the main reason why teenagers go to bed late.
Teenagers need less sleep than adults because their bodies are still growing.
Teenagers' late sleeping is largely caused by natural changes in the body, which school schedules often ignore.
Schools that start later always produce students with much higher grades.

explanation.en: The passage explains that a biological shift in the body clock makes teenagers sleepy later, and that early school timetables do not take this into account. Phones are only "part" of the story, grades rose only "slightly", and teenagers need more sleep, not less.

To: Ploy Chaiyasit
From: Naree Suwan
Subject: Your homestay in Sapporo — important information

Dear Ploy,

Thank you for confirming your place on the Winter Culture Exchange in Sapporo from 8 to 22 January. We are delighted that you will be joining twelve other students from Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia.

Your host family, the Tanakas, live about twenty minutes by subway from the language centre where your morning classes will take place. Mr and Mrs Tanaka have two children: Haruto, who is sixteen, and Yui, who is eleven. Haruto is a member of his school's English club and is very excited to practise with you. The family also has a cat, so please let us know as soon as possible if you have an allergy, as we would then need to find you another home.

Please remember that temperatures in Sapporo in January are often below minus five degrees, and snow is almost certain. Thick gloves, waterproof boots and a warm hat are essential. You do not need to buy an expensive coat before you leave, though; the programme will lend each student a winter jacket on arrival.

In the afternoons, you will take part in cultural activities such as calligraphy, a visit to a chocolate factory and the famous Snow Festival. On your final evening, each student will give a short presentation in English or Japanese about something they learned during the trip, so you may find it useful to keep a diary.

Finally, a reminder that the second payment of 18,000 baht is due by 30 November. If it has not been received by then, we cannot guarantee your place, as several students are on our waiting list.

If you have any questions, please reply to this email or call me on 02 555 0147 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays.

Best wishes,
Naree Suwan
Programme Coordinator
items.stem: What is the main purpose of the email?
choices: To invite Ploy to apply for a place on an exchange programme
To tell Ploy that her place on the programme has been cancelled
To give Ploy practical information about her trip and remind her of a payment deadline
To ask Ploy to host a Japanese student in Thailand

explanation.en: Ploy has already confirmed her place; the email gives details (host family, clothes, activities) and reminds her that the second payment is due by 30 November.
explanation.th: พลอยยืนยันที่นั่งแล้ว อีเมลนี้จึงให้ข้อมูลที่จำเป็น (ครอบครัวอุปถัมภ์ เสื้อผ้า กิจกรรม) และเตือนเรื่องกำหนดชำระเงินงวดที่สองภายใน 30 พฤศจิกายน

Less Homework, Better Learning?
by a secondary school teacher

Every evening, millions of Thai teenagers sit at their desks long after dinner, working through pages of exercises. Many parents see this as the sign of a serious school. I used to think the same. After fifteen years of teaching, however, I have become convinced that the amount of homework we give is not only unnecessary but, in many cases, harmful.

Let me be clear: I am not arguing that homework should disappear. Reading a novel, practising a musical instrument or reviewing the day's lesson for twenty minutes can all strengthen what students learn in class. The problem is quantity. When students receive assignments from six or seven teachers who do not talk to one another, the total can easily reach three or four hours a night. At that point, tired students stop thinking and start copying — from friends, from websites and, increasingly, from AI tools.

Supporters of heavy homework often argue that it teaches discipline. Discipline matters, but it can be learned in many ways: through sport, music, part-time jobs or helping at home. A student who spends every evening on worksheets has little time for any of these. Moreover, studies of students under sixteen show only a weak link between the number of hours spent on homework and exam results. Beyond about ninety minutes a night, the benefits seem to disappear altogether.

There is also a question of fairness. A child whose parents can afford a private tutor, or who has a quiet room to work in, is far better placed to complete long assignments than a child who shares a small flat with four relatives. Heavy homework, in other words, can widen the very gaps that schools are supposed to close.

What, then, should schools do? First, teachers in each year group should coordinate so that the daily total stays reasonable. Second, every assignment should have a clear purpose that students understand. Finally, schools should ask students themselves how long tasks really take; the answers are often surprising. Homework should be a tool for learning, not a test of endurance.
items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?
choices: Homework is useful in reasonable amounts, but schools should limit how much they give.
Students need more homework so that they develop discipline.
All homework should be banned because it causes stress.
Private tutors are more effective than homework.

explanation.en: The writer says "I am not arguing that homework should disappear" but that "the problem is quantity", and ends with ways to keep the total reasonable.
